decision.note: Infrastructure is useful and should improve, but it should not displace higher-priority product/research work.

strengths: Public/private portfolio boundary is explicit and registry validation enforces public-only records.
Priority score is documented as an attention-allocation score rather than a quality score.
Structured audit sidecars, a rubric, a validator, and a public evidence collector now exist.
The first structured external audit records an exact commit and separates facts, findings, limitations, and recheck triggers.
The failed high-permission one-shot bootstrap workflow has been retired.

findings.title: The repository has no explicit LICENSE
evidence: No LICENSE file was present in the repository root at the audited commit.
findings.recommendation: Choose and add an explicit license before encouraging third-party reuse. This is an owner/legal choice and should not be inferred automatically.

findings.title: Audit results are not surfaced in the GitHub Pages workbench
evidence: The dashboard is driven by portfolio/registry.json and focuses on priority/work status.
Structured audit reports now exist under audits/, but the Pages UI does not expose latest audit status, audited SHA, or open P1/P0 counts.
findings.recommendation: Add a compact audit-status layer to the workbench without conflating audit severity with portfolio priority.

findings.title: No audit staleness detection exists yet
evidence: Structured audits store audited_commit, but CI currently validates shape only.
There is no check that compares an audited commit to the repository's current default-branch head.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional public staleness check that marks audits stale when the head SHA moves, with configurable re-audit triggers.

findings.title: Static workbench sources are duplicated at repository root and under docs/
evidence: index.html, app.js, and styles.css exist at the root.
docs/index.html, docs/app.js, and docs/styles.css also exist and README documents docs/ as the Pages source.
findings.recommendation: Make docs/ the single canonical Pages source or generate one copy from the other to prevent UI drift.

findings.title: Evidence collector has no dedicated automated tests
evidence: There are no fixtures/unit tests for GitHub API parsing, action-ref pin detection, or private-repository refusal.
findings.recommendation: Add deterministic fixture-based tests with mocked API responses before expanding the collector.

findings.title: Legacy bootstrap source archive remains in the repository
evidence: .repo-auditor-bootstrap/source.part-* files remain after the bootstrap workflow was retired.
The earlier bootstrap run failed with invalid base64 before publication.
findings.recommendation: After confirming no recovery value is needed, remove the legacy archive in a separate cleanup commit.

limitations: The self-audit does not infer or choose a software license on behalf of the repository owner.
GitHub Pages visual rendering was not browser-tested in this self-audit.
Branch protection and repository administration settings were not evaluated.
The evidence collector was reviewed statically but not exercised against a large cross-language corpus.
recheck_triggers: Audit results become visible in the Pages workbench.
The root/docs static source duplication is removed.
The evidence collector gains automated fixture tests or language-specific adapters.
